endorsements.name: Seth Fogie
endorsements.label: Embedded Reverse Engineering: Cracking Mobile Binaries
endorsements.description: The embedded mobile market is headed for a day of reckoning when it will become the target of virus/trojan writers. To prepare for this, security experts must understand reverse-engineering fundamentals, as they apply to the pocket PC device, so they can research, investigate and understand the impact of malware and how to prevent it from spreading.
endorsements.subtitle: DEF CON 11

endorsements.name: Seth Fogie
endorsements.label: Attacking Windows Mobile PDAâs
endorsements.description: Attacking Windows Mobile PDAâs Microsoftâs Pocket PC (AKA Windows Mobile) has remained relatively free of all the nasty attacks that have bombarded its PC based cousins. Does this mean this OS is any more secure or safe from attack? Ironically, this is as far from the truth as one can get. Using reverse-engineering techniques, this presentation will demonstrate just how easy it is to gain full remote unauthorized access to a PPC device. In addition, we will also provide an example of a remote buffer overflow attack against the PDA and the tricks needed to place working code on the proverbial stack. This talk will be technical. However, if you want to gain a better understanding of the ARM processor, hacking Pocket PC programs, or just want to see how buffer overflow attacks work on the PDA, you will not be disappointed.

endorsements.label: CVE-2024-6749
endorsements.description:
Seth Fogie, member of the AXIS Camera Station Pro Bug Bounty Program, has found that the Incident report feature may expose sensitive credentials on the AXIS Camera Station windows client. If Incident report is not being used with credentials configured this flaw does not apply. 

 Axis has released patched versions for the highlighted flaw. Please refer to the Axis security advisory for more information and solution.
